I would assess this statement as an oversimplification, though it contains a kernel of truth when considering certain aspects of AI's function

Much like how we use Fourier transforms or principal component analysis to reduce complex vibrational data into dominant frequencies/modes, many AI models (especially generative ones) learn to capture the essence of training data distributions
Generative AI often reconstructs outputs that resemble the training data but aren't exact copies—similar to how JPEG compression retains essential features while discarding less perceptible details
A true compressor can only reconstruct what was compressed
Modern AI can synthesize novel combinations, solve unseen problems (e.g., optimizing a heat exchanger layout under new constraints), or generate designs that didn't exist in the training set
Advanced AI systems can infer causal relationships or physical principles—like understanding stress distributions or fluid dynamics from data—which goes beyond mere compression
In robotics or adaptive systems, AI makes real-time decisions based on sensor feedback, continuously interacting with a dynamic environment
This is more akin to an adaptive controller than a compression algorithm
Saying 'AI is just glorified compression' is like saying 'a turbine is just a fancy fan'
While both move fluids and share principles, a turbine extracts energy and operates under complex thermodynamic cycles—a fundamentally different function
The value lies in the emergent capabilities beyond compression
